Life cycle assessment of pond IMTA and fish polyculture

Three earthen-pond systems from the INTEGRATE project: semi-intensive pond IMTA (fish + oysters + macroalgae, Portugal), semi-extensive pond IMTA (seabream + oysters + macroalgae pond, Spain) and a conventional semi-intensive fish polyculture (fish only, Portugal). Functional unit: 1 tonne of aquatic product (fish + oyster flesh) at the farm gate, one production cycle.

Inventory and impact results are taken from INTEGRATE deliverable PI05#3 (IPMA & CTAQUA, 2020; Piscentool). The KPI framework, targets, nutrient-balance re-calculation and data checks are added in this repository.

Key findings

  1. Semi-extensive IMTA has the lowest impacts in 6 of 7 categories: global warming −56 %, energy −81 %, eutrophication −97 % against the polyculture. It takes up more nitrogen than the feed brings (net uptake).
  2. Semi-intensive IMTA vs polyculture (same site, same target density): eutrophication −57 % and water dependence −58 %, because oysters and macroalgae keep 47 % of the feed nitrogen in products (polyculture: 20 %). Global warming is almost the same (−1 %).
  3. Feed is the hotspot for global warming (55–66 %) and primary production use (>99 %). Uneaten feed and excretion (“Rejects fish”) drive acidification and eutrophication in the semi-intensive systems.
  4. Land is the trade-off: both IMTA systems need more land per tonne (+24 % and +105 %).
  5. Data checks: the tables agree (feed N, water per tonne, process sums), with two findings to clarify – the semi-extensive FCR of 0.56 includes oyster gain, and the polyculture land value does not follow the pond-area rule.

Method and sources

Primary source: INTEGRATE (2020) deliverable PI05#3, LCA of aquaculture systems: comparison between semi-intensive/extensive pond IMTA and semi-intensive traditional fishpond production (Interreg Atlantic Area EAPA_232/2016; IPMA, CTAQUA). Nutrient emissions: Cho & Kaushik (1990). Software: Piscentool (Wilfart et al. 2012). Methodological background: Hala, Chougule et al. (2024), Aquaculture 590, 741035. Inventory shared in the LCIS2024 structure (Nair, Chougule et al. 2025, J. Clean. Prod. 520, 146120).
